sections.text:
What is Friction?
The effort customers experience when
interacting with your brand.
It is the painful barrier that keeps humans from
achieving their desired outcomes.
EAS measures 4 types of Effort:
What is EAS?
EAS is a first of its kind tool that integrates
traditional research methods and neuroscience
to measure customer effort.
Physical:
When achieving a
desired outcome
requires customers to
take physicaleffort.
Time:
When a customer
must go through long
waiting periods to
achieve an outcome.
Cognitive:
When processes and
touchpoints increase
the cognitive load of
customers.
Perceived:
When customers perceive the
amount of friction involved in
an outcome to be higher than
what it may turn out to be.

sections.text:
How it
works
Declarative assessment
Measures transactional Customer Effort
for the following dimensions: Time,
Physical, Cognitive & Perceived.
Non-declarative assessment
Focused on eliciting emotional
associations and emotional
components of effort for two
dimensions: Emotional and Cognitive.
The Score
The Score integrates implicit testing responses and qualitative declarative answers.
It provides a break up of effort across the three components of Time, Physical and
Cognitive Effort. It also provides the associated emotions.
+

Secondary research
- Best practices from adjacent industries

- Physical, Time & Cognitive Effort scores for the journey
Recommendations
